title: VS Code extension refuses to connect to a daemon whose /health reports another project
description:
Follow-up from task-e7f4026a (HIGH, a seat adopted another project's daemon through a stale daemon.json). That bug's description asks to check "the IDE plugins' daemon adoption". Its DoD covers JetBrains only (task-90664db1), so this row is the VS Code parity. It lands in BACKLOG for the human to schedule.

The gap, checked by the planning architect on 2026-10-30, is wider than in JetBrains. moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts ensureDaemonRunning() and waitForDaemonInfo():
- compare only the projectPath written in .moe/daemon.json (pathsMatch);
- then trust isPortOpen(host, port), with no PID check at all.
So once this project's daemon dies and another project's daemon takes the recorded port, connect() opens ws://<host>:<port>/ws to the other project's board.

Deliverable:
- Before connect() opens /ws, probe http://<host>:<port>/health with a bounded timeout and a body capped at 64 KiB. Compare its projectPath by the comparable-path rule of packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts comparableProjectPath (D:\x == D:/x == /mnt/d/x).
- On a foreign reply:
  - open no client;
  - treat daemon.json as stale, deleting it only while it still names the pid, port and startedAt that were read;
  - log and show which project that daemon serves;
  - start this project's daemon, which takes the next free port.
- An unknown reply (unreachable, non-JSON, oversize, no projectPath) keeps today's behavior.
- Mirror the decisions landed by the JetBrains fix (task-90664db1): read its code and handoff memory first.
- Tests in moe-vscode/tests. The vm harnesses transpile single files with a closed require shim (mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness), so check which harnesses load MoeDaemonClient.ts before adding an import to it.

Ordering: MoeDaemonClient.ts is in CQ-RF06's and CQ-RF06b's plans (task-98ffe33f, task-032c9739). This row dependsOn both, plus the JetBrains fix.

Not in scope: the proxy, the wrappers, the JetBrains plugin, the daemon.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile
definitionOfDone: A daemon at the port .moe/daemon.json names, whose /health projectPath is another project, gets no /ws client from the extension. The stale daemon.json is removed only while it still names the pid, port and startedAt that were read, and this project's daemon is started. Proven by a moe-vscode test.
This project's path in any spelling (D:\x, D:/x, /mnt/d/x) counts as the same project. Unreachable, non-JSON, oversize and projectPath-less /health replies keep today's behavior. Proven by test rows.
`cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.
